To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the majority of the coverage of the tanning issue in magazines targeted toward girls, young women and older women focused on the benefits of tanning, (2) the coverage of tanned appearance as a benefit of tanning increased between 1998 and 2006, and (3) the coverage of the prevention-relevant issues also increased during this period.
the coverage of the benefits of tanning bed usage increased during the 1997– 2006 period, while the coverage of the consequences of tanning bed exposure increased as well.
the coverage of the risks of tanning and the prevention methods was low, whereas the coverage of tanned skin benefits was high, especially in magazines targeting younger readers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the potential influence of media coverage on the beliefs of young and older women regarding tanning bed use and the potential impact on skin cancer prevention.
the mediated environment that may affect the health behaviors of women.
the mediated communication environment and its potential influence on tanning behaviors and beliefs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in general, the media environment surrounding women's tanning behavior was not optimal.
the mediated communication environment of the 8 magazines was not effective at reducing tanning bed use.
the coverage of the tanning risks and preventive measures was not enough to counterbalance the tanning benefits.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the coverage of the tanning bed risk and prevention issues in magazines targeting women was not sufficient to counteract the positive coverage of tanning.
the media coverage of tanning is more likely to focus on the positive aspects of tanning than the negative consequences.
the mediated environment that surrounds women's tanning behavior is a mixed bag.
The main takeaway from our work is that
tanning bed use is a health risk that is not being adequately addressed in magazines targeting women.
tanning benefits were more frequently covered than tanning risks and prevention methods in popular magazines that target female readers.
the mediated communication environment may contribute to the maintenance of the tanning behavior among women.
